name: selinux-policy-tools
description: Navigation and authoring help for refpolicy-style SELinux policy source (RHEL/Fedora selinux-policy, CLIP-style locked-down policies).

selinux.extraIncludePaths.description: Additional directories to index (e.g. a full selinux-policy checkout when you work on local modules in a separate folder).

selinux.useDevelHeaders.description: Index the installed selinux-policy-devel headers. 'auto' does so only when the workspace has no support macros (i.e. you are writing standalone modules).

selinux.develHeadersPath.description: Location of the selinux-policy-devel interface headers.

selinux.diagnostics.unknownMacros.description: Warn about calls to interfaces/templates/macros that are not defined anywhere in the index.

selinux.diagnostics.classPerms.description: Check object classes and permissions in allow/dontaudit/auditallow/neverallow rules against the flask definitions.

selinux.diagnostics.genRequire.description: Warn about missing requires: in .if files, a type or attribute used in an interface but missing from its gen_require block; in .te files of loadable modules, a type or attribute from another module used without a require in its scope, and requirements outside optional_policy that only modules turned off in modules.conf provide (the link would fail).

selinux.diagnostics.users.description: Check gen_user() lines: roles that are not declared anywhere, MLS/MCS levels and categories outside what the build defines, a range whose high level is below its low level, and users defined twice.

selinux.build.enabled.description: Compile with the real toolchain to report compiler and link errors and show what each line compiles to. A standalone module directory is built against selinux-policy-devel; a refpolicy source tree is built with its own Makefile. Needs Linux with make, m4, checkpolicy and policycoreutils-devel.

selinux.build.onSave.description: Build when a policy file is saved (a check: nothing is written next to your sources). The SELinux: Build command also packages a standalone module as <module>.pp.

selinux.build.develMakefile.description: Makefile used to build standalone modules.

selinux.build.tree.makeArgs.markdownDescription: Extra `make` variables for full source-tree builds, overriding `build.conf`. Use what your policy RPM passes, e.g. for CLIP: `["NAME=mcs", "TYPE=mcs", "DISTRO=redhat", "UBAC=y", "MONOLITHIC=n", "UNK_PERMS=deny", "APPS_MODS=ssh postfix ..."]`.

selinux.build.tree.targets.markdownDescription: Make targets for source-tree builds. Empty: `base.pp modules`, then `validate` (or `policy` when `MONOLITHIC=y`).

selinux.build.tree.validate.markdownDescription: After a modular tree compiles, run `make validate` (link all modules, expand, check file contexts) to catch modules that require types from disabled modules. Adds a few seconds; its results arrive after the compile results.

selinux.build.tree.outputDir.markdownDescription: Where the **SELinux: Build** command copies a full tree's outputs (module packages, `policy.bin`, file contexts, plus `build-info.json`). `~/…` is your home directory; a relative path is under the tree root. Empty: outputs stay in a scratch directory that is removed when VS Code closes. Builds on save never write here.

from.description: modules.conf to start from (relative to the tree root, or absolute)

disable.description: List files (one module per line, # comments); every non-base module named in them is turned off, as the RHEL 10 spec's process-modules-filtered.py does

from.description: modules.conf to start from (relative to the tree root, or absolute)

disable.description: List files (one module per line, # comments); every non-base module named in them is turned off, as the RHEL 10 spec's process-modules-filtered.py does

selinux.build.tree.files.markdownDescription: Files to put into the scratch copy of a full tree before building, as `"tree/relative/path": "source"` or `["source1", "source2"]` (concatenated). A source can also be `{ "from": "dist/targeted/modules.conf", "disable": ["…/modules-dropped.lst"] }`: that file with every non-base module named in the lists turned off (how the RHEL 10 spec builds modules.conf). Your tree is not modified. Used for config a policy RPM puts in place at build time, e.g. RHEL's `policy/modules.conf`, `policy/booleans.conf` and `policy/users`. `~/…` is your home directory; relative sources are under the tree root. *SELinux: Configure Build from Spec File…* fills this in (RHEL 9 and RHEL 10 spec layouts).

selinux.ifdef.evaluate.markdownDescription: Decide `ifdef`/`ifndef` blocks on m4 build flags (`enable_mcs`, `enable_mls`, `distro_redhat`, …) the way the configured build would, asking the Makefile for its flags (Linux, trusted workspaces). Inactive branches are dimmed, ignored by diagnostics, and their definitions leave the index. `ifdef` on other names (interface names, `define()`d or undefined names) is decided from where the sources define them; dynamically defined names stay undecided.

selinux.checks.file.markdownDescription: Property checks file, relative to the policy tree root (for a standalone module: the workspace folder; it is checked against the module linked with the installed policy). Each line is an assertion about the compiled policy (`only X may write T`, `never X may read T`, `never X reaches Y`, `never T flows to U`, `require X may append T:file`), checked after every build and whenever the file is saved. See the README.

selinux.build.trees.markdownDescription: Build settings per policy tree, for workspaces with several trees: `{ "rhel10": { "makeArgs": [...], "files": {...} } }`, keyed by the tree path (relative to the workspace folder, or absolute). An entry overrides `selinux.build.tree.*` (`makeArgs`, `files`, `targets`, `validate`, `outputDir`) while that tree is active. *SELinux: Configure Build from Spec File…* writes here when the workspace has several trees.

selinux.tree.autoSwitch.markdownDescription: With several policy trees in the workspace, switch to the tree of the file you open (indexing, diagnostics, builds and views follow it). Otherwise switch with *SELinux: Select Policy Tree…* (or the status bar item).

viewsWelcome.contents:
No SELinux policy sources found in this workspace. Open a policy source tree or a folder with a module (.te, .if, .fc).
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
New to SELinux Policy Tools? Try a practice module with a few deliberate mistakes, or follow the tutorials.
[Create Practice Module](command:selinux.createPracticeModule)
[Open Tutorials](command:selinux.openTutorials)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with SELinux Policy Tools
walkthroughs.description: Navigate, check and build refpolicy-style SELinux policy, and see what it really compiles to.

steps.title: What this extension does
steps.description:
Source navigation and checks, real builds, and tools to review and lock down policy. Open a policy tree or module folder, or start with a practice module that has four deliberate mistakes.
[Create Practice Module](command:selinux.createPracticeModule)
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

steps.title: Set up the Linux host
steps.description:
Builds run the real SELinux toolchain on Linux; from Windows or macOS, use Remote-SSH. Install the tools once and trust the workspace.
[Open a Terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)

steps.title: Find your way around
steps.description:
Hover, F12, Shift+F12 and Ctrl+T work on interfaces, types and template-generated names. The Policy Explorer lists every module.
[Show the Policy Explorer](command:selinuxPolicyExplorer.focus)
[Open a Module…](command:selinux.findModule)

steps.title: Fix problems as you type
steps.description:
Unknown interfaces, wrong permissions, missing requires and more, with quick fixes (Ctrl+.). The practice module has four mistakes to fix.
[Show Problems](command:workbench.actions.view.problems)

steps.title: Build and see what a line grants
steps.description:
Saving builds with the real toolchain; errors land on the right line. After a build, hover an interface call to see the rules it compiled to.
[Build](command:selinux.buildModule)
[Show Expanded Policy](command:selinux.showExpanded)

steps.title: Work on a full policy tree
steps.description:
Trees are built with their own Makefile. For RHEL and Fedora trees, take the build settings from the RPM spec.
[Configure Build from Spec File…](command:selinux.configureFromSpec)
[Select Policy Tree…](command:selinux.selectTree)

steps.title: Browse the compiled policy
steps.description:
The policy as the kernel sees it after the last build: types, attributes, roles, and every rule traced back to the source line that grants it.
[Show Compiled Policy](command:selinuxCompiledPolicy.focus)
[Find in Compiled Policy](command:selinux.findInPolicy)

steps.title: Where to go next
steps.description:
Three more walkthroughs: writing a service policy, fixing denials, and reviewing and locking down a policy.
[Write a Service Policy](command:selinux.openTutorials?%5B%22services%22%5D)
[Fix a Denial](command:selinux.openTutorials?%5B%22denials%22%5D)
[Review and Lock Down](command:selinux.openTutorials?%5B%22lockdown%22%5D)

walkthroughs.title: Write and maintain a service policy
walkthroughs.description: Confine a daemon with the service editor: files, ports, system access, booleans and helper programs, then edit it safely later.

steps.title: Before you start: what does the service need?
steps.description: A confined service gets only what its policy lists. Gather its program, files, ports and the system services it uses.

steps.title: Open the service editor
steps.description:
A form with a live preview of the .te, .if and .fc it writes. Hover anything for an explanation.
[New Service…](command:selinux.newService)

steps.title: Give it files of its own
steps.description: One type per kind of file (runtime, state, logs, configuration, …) with the lowest access that works. Type transitions are set up for you.

steps.title: Network: ports it serves and uses
steps.description: Pick port types to listen on and connect to, or create a new port type for a port number nothing covers yet.

steps.title: System access, capabilities and interfaces
steps.description: Common needs in plain words (logging, name lookups, D-Bus, TLS certificates…), root capabilities, and any other interface.

steps.title: Optional rights with booleans
steps.description: Rights only some sites need go under a boolean that administrators switch on with setsebool.

steps.title: Split off helper programs
steps.description: Programs the service runs can get a domain of their own, with fewer (or different) rights than the service.

steps.title: Create, install and test
steps.description:
Create the module, install and label it, test in permissive mode and fix the denials before enforcing.
[Install Module](command:selinux.installModule)

steps.title: Change it later, safely
steps.description:
Open any service module in the same form: only the lines of changed settings are edited. Review the compiled effect before committing.
[Edit Service…](command:selinux.editService)
[Compare with HEAD](command:selinux.compareHead)

walkthroughs.title: Fix a denial the right way
walkthroughs.description: From an AVC message to a minimal, reviewed fix: read it, find the cause, grant with an interface, verify what you granted.

steps.title: Read the denial
steps.description:
Who (scontext), what (permission), on what (tclass and tcontext): one sentence. The denial assistant reads them for you and says whether a rule is really missing.
[Analyze Denials…](command:selinux.analyzeDenials)
[Open a Terminal](command:workbench.action.terminal.new)

steps.title: Is the policy wrong, or the label?
steps.description:
Many denials are mislabeled files, booleans that are off, or harmless probes. The denial assistant checks those first.
[Analyze Denials…](command:selinux.analyzeDenials)
[Find in Compiled Policy](command:selinux.findInPolicy)

steps.title: Grant it with an interface
steps.description:
The module that owns the type has an interface for it. Find it with completion, hover and the interface search.
[Open a Module…](command:selinux.findModule)

steps.title: Check what you actually granted
steps.description:
Hover the call for the rules it compiled to, compare the compiled policy with HEAD, and guard the result with a property check.
[Compare with HEAD](command:selinux.compareHead)
[Open Property Checks](command:selinux.openChecks)

walkthroughs.title: Review and lock down a policy
walkthroughs.description: Review compiled changes, turn modules off safely, follow domain transitions and keep security properties checked after every build.

steps.title: What did this change grant?
steps.description:
Compare the compiled policy with HEAD, a release tag, two refs or a saved build: every permission, traced to source.
[Compare with HEAD](command:selinux.compareHead)
[Compare with…](command:selinux.compareWith)

steps.title: Turn modules off without surprises
steps.description:
Preview link errors, optional blocks that drop out and rule changes before editing modules.conf.
[Preview a Module Off/On…](command:selinux.previewModule)

steps.title: Who can become whom
steps.description:
The domain transition graph of the compiled policy: which domains can reach which.
[Show Transition Graph](command:selinux.transitionGraph)

steps.title: Security properties, checked every build
steps.description:
Write requirements like "never user_t reaches sysadm_t" once; they are re-checked after every build and failures traced to source.
[Open Property Checks](command:selinux.openChecks)

steps.title: Compare with what is installed
steps.description:
What would change on this host if you installed your build, including local customizations you would lose.
[Compare with Installed Policy](command:selinux.compareInstalled)

steps.title: Users, roles and MLS levels
steps.description:
gen_user lines are checked as you type; the Compiled Policy view shows users, roles and logins.
[Show Compiled Policy](command:selinuxCompiledPolicy.focus)

steps.title: A lockdown routine
steps.description: Preview, apply, build, check, compare: a repeatable way to shrink and harden a policy.

scripts.test: node test/lsp-e2e.js && node test/ifelse-test.js && node test/ifdef-names-test.js && node test/service-test.js && node test/denials-test.js && node test/walkthrough-test.js

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In Restricted Mode, navigation and diagnostics work but policy builds are off, because building runs the policy tree's Makefile.
